title: Neighbor stability and slice probes for embeddings onboarding
content:
Purpose:
This is a working labbook for a set of lightweight, reproducible probes we can run when onboarding new embedding models (open or finetuned) into Redwood inference. The focus is on:
- neighbor stability across smallish query perturbations (robustness),
- targeted slice probes for semantic search relevance (long-tail / ambiguity / code-switch), and
- clustering sanity checks for multilingual mixed corpora.

Why this doc exists (quick):
- current embed onboarding covers bulk metrics (avg cosine distributions, P@k on core tasks) but misses brittle slices and neighbor rearrangements that often correlate with production regressions.
- want a compact, repeatable set of tests to catch regressions early and provide concrete failure modes for model/product owners.

High-level protocol (summary):
1) sample a small standardized probe corpus (~3k examples) with labeled slices (see sampling below).
2) compute neighbor sets (k=50) for each item with model-A and model-B (baseline vs candidate).
3) compute neighbor-stability metrics, slice-level relevance metrics, clustering sanity checks.
4) triage items above/below thresholds via quick human annotation.
5) produce a one-page regression brief with top N failures + recommended mitigations.

Sampling + dataset composition (recommended):
- total size: ~3k items (fits in quick on-host evals and human review).
- composition by slice (approx):
  - 30% generic QA/FAQ-style short queries (wiki/KB sentences)
  - 20% long-form context passages (300-600 chars)
  - 15% paraphrase pairs / near-duplicates (synthetic + crowd)
  - 10% code-switched / language-mix (EN+ES, EN+ZH, EN+HI samples)
  - 10% named-entity-heavy (legal, finance, product names)
  - 10% ambiguous short queries (single-token or pronoun heavy)
  - 5% synthetic adversarial noise (typos, punctuation drops)

Notes on multilingual sampling: prioritize language pairs representative of APAC/EU usage (EN-ES, EN-ZH, EN-FR, EN-HI). For cross-lingual alignment probes, include translation anchor pairs (source sentence + professional translation) so we can measure alignment consistency rather than raw retrieval.

Metrics (compute per-slice and overall):
- Neighbor Jaccard (top-k overlap): Jaccard(top-k(model-A), top-k(model-B)) per item => aggregate median and tail (5th percentile).
- Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) / P@k / NDCG for labeled relevance judgments (semantic search queries).
- Neighbor Drift Score: fraction of items whose nearest neighbor (k=1) changes domain (e.g., from same-article to different-article) between models.
- Silhouette-ish cluster sanity: run HDBSCAN on embeddings for small topical batches and compute purity + number of spurious micro-clusters.
- Cross-lingual anchor alignment: cosine difference distribution between translation pairs vs random pairs.
- Length-sensitivity curve: P@10 / MRR stratified by query length buckets (short < 16 chars, mid 16-120, long > 120).

Acceptance / regression thresholds (working defaults):
- Median neighbor Jaccard (k=10) vs baseline should not drop by > 0.10.
- 5th percentile neighbor Jaccard should not drop by > 0.25 (we care about tail stability).
- Slice-level P@10 drop > 0.05 triggers slice investigation (especially on named-entity and code-switch slices).
- Cross-lingual anchor alignment mean cosine drop > 0.03 flagged.
- Any increase in number of spurious micro-clusters (>25% relative increase) requires manual review.

Labeling / annotation protocol (for quick triage):
- Task: given query Q and candidate passage P, label relevance on 3-point scale: 2 (good/precise answer), 1 (related but incomplete), 0 (irrelevant).
- For clustering sanity: annotators shown 8 nearest neighbours for a seed item and asked whether cluster is coherent (yes/no + brief reason).
- Annotator notes: use "source-preservation" check for multilingual anchors (translation should be semantically equivalent; cultural/localization differences noted in comments).

Human rater prompts (example):
- "Does passage P answer the user intent expressed in query Q directly?"
- "Are the top 4 neighbours for item X all about the same concrete entity/topic? If not, mark incoherent and note drift type (topic merge / noise / duplicate)."

Automated diagnostics to include in brief:
- Top 20 items with largest neighbor Jaccard delta (with context and nearest neighbours from both models).
- Top slice-wise metric deltas + per-slice histograms.
- Example clusters that split/merge compared to baseline showing centroid examples.
- For multilingual: translation-anchor pairs that moved from top-1 to beyond top-20.

Quick triage workflow (for engineering/product review):
- Run probe job (script produces HTML diagnostics and csv of flagged items).
- Product owner reviews top 10 flagged items and marks severity (high/medium/low).
- If high severity, create targeted eval set for A/B and consider mitigation: finetune, prompt-synthetic augmentation, or fallback routing to more robust model variant.

Implementation notes / scripts (references):
- lightweight python runner: embeddings_eval/neighbor_probe/run_probe.py (see linked GitHub).
- precompute index with faiss flat index (k=200) to keep deterministic neighbor sets.
- store canonical seeds and RNG seeds to make runs repeatable.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final k for neighbor stability tests (10 vs 50): k=10 better for product-facing retrieval; k=50 exposes more recall-related shifts. Maybe run both.
- Determine sampling refresh cadence: monthly? after every deployed model?
- Annotator pool: use in-house ML annotators vs contracted vendors for multilingual quality.
- Add synthetic paraphrase generator for low-resource languages so slices are balanced.

Quick example failure vignette (for context):
- Baseline model-A returns an exact duplicate paragraph from same KB page as top-1. Candidate model-B returns a high-cosine neighbour from a different article because it over-weights surface n-gram match. Neighbor Jaccard falls from 0.9->0.3. P@1 drops and user-visible search results degrade. Root causes to check: tokenization changes, sentence-piece vocab diffs, or training corpus domain gap.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact (we want fast cycles). The aim is not to fully replace larger eval suites, but to add a focused set of probes that map cleanly to operational mitigations.
- Please comment on thresholds and slice definitions — especially people with recent on-call/regression experience.

- 2025-02-18: refined thresholds + added cluster-spike metric (Carlos).
